questions.q: A company has never used Amazon Q. It wants a managed AI assistant that lets employees ask questions over SharePoint and Confluence content, with answers that respect each user's document permissions. Which service should it adopt?

options.t: Amazon Quick, with ACL-enabled knowledge bases
options.why: Right: Quick is the recommended successor for new customers and supports document-level ACLs on SharePoint and Confluence Cloud knowledge bases.

options.t: Amazon Q Business
options.why: Wrong: it fits the need, but it is no longer open to new customers.

options.t: Amazon Q Developer
options.why: Wrong: it is an assistant for building and operating on AWS, not an employee assistant over company documents.

options.t: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with a custom UI
options.why: Wrong: that is the build-your-own path, more work than a finished employee assistant.

questions.explain: New employee-assistant projects go to Amazon Quick; Q Business is closed to new customers.
questions.remember: Employee assistant over company data, new customer → Amazon Quick. Q Business only for existing customers (run, secure, migrate).
variants: The company already runs Q Business → keep it, or move to Quick with BYOI.
The team wants its own RAG backend or custom UI → Bedrock Knowledge Bases + AgentCore.
Developers want help in the AWS console → Amazon Q Developer.

questions.q: A company runs Amazon Q Business with a large index. It wants employees to use Amazon Quick quickly, without re-crawling all its data sources, while Q Business keeps running. Both are in the same account and Region. What should it do?

options.t: Re-create every data source as a native Quick connector and re-ingest
options.why: Wrong: it works, but re-crawls all the data, which the company wants to avoid.

options.t: Use BYOI to connect the existing Q Business index as a Quick knowledge base
options.why: Right: BYOI reuses the index with no re-crawl and Q Business runs in parallel; it needs the same account and Region.

options.t: Export the index to S3 and load it into Quick with an MCP integration
options.why: Wrong: MCP integrations support actions, not knowledge-base indexing.

options.t: Share the index with Quick through a Q Business data accessor
options.why: Wrong: data accessors share the index with verified ISVs, not the migration path to Quick.

questions.explain: BYOI connects an existing Q index to Quick with no re-crawl.
questions.remember: Existing Q Business → Quick fast, no re-crawl → BYOI (same account and Region). BYOI does NOT carry Q Apps, Actions or chat guardrails.
variants: The Q Apps must keep working → recreate them as Quick Flows (forms not yet supported).
BYOI is used in non-IDC mode and users see too much → split content into separate knowledge bases and set permissions per space.
A third index is needed in the Region → BYOI allows at most 2 Q Business indexes per Region, not increasable.

questions.q: A data engineering team wants AWS Budgets alerts to appear in its Slack channel with the least custom code. Which approach fits?

options.t: A Lambda function that polls Cost Explorer and posts to a Slack webhook
options.why: Wrong: it works, but it is custom code to write and run.

options.t: Amazon Q Business with a Slack integration
options.why: Wrong: that is an employee assistant over company data, not an AWS notification relay.

options.t: Budgets alerts to an SNS topic, delivered by Amazon Q Developer in chat applications
options.why: Right: Q Developer in chat applications forwards AWS notifications such as Budgets alerts to Slack or Teams channels.

options.t: CloudTrail logs to a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter
options.why: Wrong: CloudTrail records API activity; it does not deliver budget alerts to chat.

questions.explain: SNS + Amazon Q Developer in chat applications relays AWS alerts to Slack/Teams.
questions.remember: AWS alerts into Slack or Microsoft Teams → SNS topic + Amazon Q Developer in chat applications. Restrict chat users with channel guardrails and per-channel IAM roles.
variants: Alerts by email only → SNS email subscription.
Unexpected spend patterns, not fixed thresholds → Cost Anomaly Detection, delivered the same way.
Chat users must not run broad actions → channel guardrails and scoped IAM roles per channel.

questions.q: In an existing Amazon Q Business application, users report that answers only ever use public documents, even for content they can open in the source system. What is the most likely cause?

options.t: The application is set to answer from enterprise data only
options.why: Wrong: that blocks LLM-knowledge answers; it does not hide permitted enterprise documents.

options.t: The index has hit its query-per-second quota
options.why: Wrong: exceeding QPS causes throttling, not public-only answers.

options.t: The users have Lite instead of Pro subscriptions
options.why: Wrong: Lite still includes permission-aware Q&A; Pro adds Q Apps and plugins.

options.t: The data source has no email-based ACLs, or the user's email is missing
options.why: Right: Q Business filters documents by the user's email identity; without it, only public documents are used.

questions.explain: Q Business matches users to document ACLs by email; no match means public documents only.
questions.remember: Q Business answers follow document ACLs matched by user email. Public-only answers → fix connector ACLs or identity (email) mapping.
variants: Users are throttled → index QPS (default 1) exceeded; request an increase.
"Couldn't find an answer" → content not synced, enterprise-only mode, or no access.
A user sees no Apps tab → Lite subscription, Q Apps disabled, or a Region without Q Apps.

questions.q: A pipeline engineer used Amazon Q Developer to generate the IAM policy for a new Glue job role. What should the team do before deploying it?

options.t: Review the policy for least privilege and test it, as with any IaC
options.why: Right: AI output can be wrong or too broad, so generated IAM policies and IaC must be reviewed for least privilege.

options.t: Deploy it as is, because Q Developer is augmented with AWS content
options.why: Wrong: grounding in AWS content does not make the output correct or minimal.

options.t: Attach `AdministratorAccess` to be safe and trim it later
options.why: Wrong: this is the opposite of least privilege.

options.t: Paste the job's database credentials into the chat so Q can scope the policy
options.why: Wrong: never paste secrets or PII into an AI assistant.

questions.explain: Treat AI-generated IAM and IaC like any other code: review for least privilege, test, and code-review it.
questions.remember: AI-generated IAM policies or IaC → review for least privilege, run tests and normal code review; never paste secrets or PII into the assistant.
variants: The team wants vulnerabilities flagged in pipeline code while coding → Q Developer IDE security scan plus normal static analysis.
Q Developer must be blocked in some accounts → SCPs.
Users need console chat access → IAM permissions such as the `AmazonQDeveloperAccess` managed policy.
